你有你的白宫超级智能峰会，
我有我的首尔Hyperliquid峰会。

今天的 KBW 主会场访谈，jeff 还是输出了不少新观点，我提炼了几段印象深刻的：

1）加密本来就是全球资产，传统交易所从 24/5 往 24/7 走，说明需求是真的。

2）链上的价值不在交易时间，而在两点：用户自己掌握资产，以及透明带来的中立。

3）下一个机会是私募市场。财富大多在私募阶段创造，让全球尽早对它们做价格发现，才有机会打破这个格局。

4）资产代币化还没起飞，谁能赢不好说，这也是中立基础设施的美：不是谁大谁赢，小团队同样有机会。

@chameleon_jeff 说的这段最有感触：Hyperliquid 不是某家公司的生意。 是一群贡献者和用户，一起搭一个大家共有、不被资本 (私人利益) 左右的金融系统。

Interview Summary: 24/7 Trading on Hyperliquid (@Joonylive  × Jeff Yan)

Joony Koo: Two years ago, the prevailing view was that markets should close because of risk, rest, and off-hours liquidity. Was there a moment when that view broke for you?

Jeff Yan: Crypto is an inherently international asset, so the idea of market hours never really fit, and 24/7 has always been the default. It started to matter for traditional assets when the incumbent exchanges began extending their hours. They didn't go straight to 24/7, they went to 24/5, but it became clear they had recognized customer demand and were responding to it.

Joony Koo: Incumbents are now matching the hours. What is left that an on-chain venue can offer?

Jeff Yan: Trading hours are independent of being on-chain. The core of on-chain finance is two things. First, users keep control and custody of their funds. That doesn't matter day to day, but it matters in critical moments, when counterparties, intermediaries, or custodians run into trouble. Reducing trust assumptions and moving power to individuals rather than a single point of failure makes the system more robust. Second, transparency. It has limited mass appeal, but being able to know, in theory, everything happening in the system brings a trust and neutrality you don't get from a system controlled by one private organization. You can have 24/7 trading without these properties, but these are what on-chain markets can offer the world.

Joony Koo: This year commodities, equities, and pre-IPO names traded at scale, and price discovery sometimes happened while the reference markets were closed. What did the team learn from watching the two run side by side?

Jeff Yan: The clearest lesson is that demand for 24/7 trading exists. You wouldn't know without these markets, but the world doesn't sleep as a whole. Global 24/7 markets concentrate liquidity across more buyers and sellers, making markets more efficient and liquid for everyone. There will always be someone, somewhere, who wants to express a view, so once the option exists, those markets become the Schelling point where people go to do that.

Joony Koo: HIP-3 lets independent teams create markets, and institutions are building on top too. If anyone can build, what is Labs focusing on?

Jeff Yan: Labs specializes in the technology and infrastructure that supports deployers. What a deployer needs varies widely depending on who they are, where they're based, who their users are, and what they want to list, and the list is long. The vision is for Hyperliquid to be a neutral infrastructure layer, like AWS, which spared startups and large firms from reinventing the wheel. Financial primitives like order books should become pervasive and battle-tested infrastructure, and making that work for everyone is the primary mandate.

Joony Koo: The "AWS for finance" analogy reminds me of working at a game company when people debated whether the cloud could be trusted. What open problems would Labs most like to see others solve?

Jeff Yan: First, builders should find something they're uniquely positioned to do, given their interests and competitive advantages, and we'll support whatever they build. One specific hard problem is tokenizing the underlying assets themselves. Custody, liquidity, and the mechanics are all harder, so it hasn't taken off yet. I hope to see strong projects and builders next year, because having the assets represented on-chain synergizes with price discovery and liquidity.

Joony Koo: Tokenization is speeding up as more institutions get involved. Any advice for smaller teams?

Jeff Yan: Many teams, big and small, are working on tokenization, but it hasn't hit escape velocity and it's unclear who will succeed. That's the beauty of neutral infrastructure: you don't win just because you're big, though big teams may have legitimate advantages like institutional connectivity. Viral products often come from small teams that see the world differently and think less rigidly. Perps are intuitive and fair instruments that concentrate liquidity across the globe and across all time horizons into one asset, so they're easy to present to users. Some small team may even reinvent how the interfaces look.

Joony Koo: You spent three days with the Korean community this week. What stood out?

Jeff Yan: Like last year, I felt the hospitality, and I'm grateful to everyone who organized events. The community here is strong, and trading is a core part of many Koreans' lives, so it was great to discuss how on-chain markets and HIP-3 would change their approach to markets. Talking to users and the community inspires us to keep building.

Joony Koo: And your meetings with institutions?

Jeff Yan: It's cool to see institutions interested in the platform and building on top of it. They're understandably slower to adopt new technology because they have a lot to protect, but as this year has shown, the appetite is significant.

Joony Koo: Last question: what is next to be priced 24/7 that has no continuous price today?

Jeff Yan: Nothing specific, but private markets are a big opportunity, and you already see some of it through HIP-3 deployers. Much wealth creation happens privately, because companies have incentives to stay private as long as possible. It isn't intended to exclude most of the world's population, but that's what happens in practice. Allowing global price discovery on these assets as early as possible, in a global system not confined to one jurisdiction, could break that trend. There are many complexities to work through, but markets exist so everyone can benefit from them, and trading anything, anytime, anywhere has the most potential here.

Joony Koo: Any final remarks?

Jeff Yan: Hyperliquid's core strength is its community and people. It's not one company doing what's best for itself, but a decentralized network of contributors and users building a financial system owned by the people rather than by private interests. There's a long way to go and many challenges, but seeing everyone in Seoul, I feel we're in good hands, and we'll build something the financial system can ultimately adopt.

@kbwofficial @HyperliquidX

当年 @colinwu 采访 jeff 说，问了一个问题：HYPE 上线时为什么没上任何 CEX？

@chameleon_jeff 的回答是：

我们的框架一直专注于构建和创造用户想要的东西，不太在乎别人怎么做。我们只是专注，彻底专注于正在做的事。团队很小，没有 BD；有人负责社区和生态，但没有像别的公司那样面向机构的全职团队。

所以没有足够资源去处理上市。每个平台自己决定上不上，我们都能接受任何结果。有平台想上我们的代币，那很棒——他们的用户会接触到产品；不上也没关系，只要技术做好，之后他们也可能上。真正关心 Hyperliquid 的人会主动找到我们。

假设有热心用户很在意却找不到我们、自己去试一下，这也不是坏结果。根本原因只是：我们没有能力做超出核心职能的事情。

之前在 When Shift Happens 播客中主持人就问过 jeff 相关的问题：员工解锁会不会每个月往市场上灌数亿美元？jeff 的回答是——这不应成为公共审视的对象，也不是他的职责去评判或披露。

当时看到这段我是觉得 jeff 说得很公允。游戏规则一开始就讲好了的，不想玩的人可以不玩，何况团队实际情况是更为克制。再者，代币一旦归属到团队成员的名下，就是他们的个人资产了，他们怎么处置的确是他们的自由。只是链上完全透明，肯定还是会有好奇宝宝去追踪流向，也许可以指导交易决策。

反正，只观察，不评判。

这次准备放开 HIP-3 Funding Clamp，又是精细活。jeff 发的公告几乎没解释是什么，因为涉及的机制挺复杂、没那么好理解。

简单理解是——

Perp 是靠“资金费率”把合约价往真价上拽。HIP-3 的资金费率都是由四个变量决定的，之前唯有变量 clamp (夹紧区间) 是限死的，默认的是加密盘的灵敏度，其实对股票、外汇、原油这些市场不友好。

现在 clamp 可以让部署者按 perp 品类自行设置参数了，离 House of All Finance 又近了一步👨‍🍳

quoted.text:
小夫厨房开餐喽，新饭端上来了🍳

Hyperliquid 要开放一个影响持仓成本的关键参数，HIP-3 部署方将获得更多的资金费率控制权✅

根据 Jeff 9月11日的社区公告，下一次网络升级后，部署方可以自行设置 funding clamp。这个看起来很技术性的更新，值得关注👇

1/3 什么变化？

官方接口已列出 setFundingClamps，支持按标的设置：

• 可调范围：0–1%
• 默认值：0.03%
• 参数采用8小时口径，资金费仍按小时结算。

部署方此前已有利率项、费率倍率两项工具，这次进一步开放了公式内的调节参数。

2/3 对持仓有什么影响？

clamp 决定资金费率在多大程度上向利率基准靠拢。数值越大，费率维持在基准附近的缓冲区越宽；数值越小，费率越容易随合约溢价、折价变化。

举个简化例子：假设平均溢价0.10%、利率项0.01%、倍率1，按8小时口径计算：

• clamp＝0.03% → 资金费率0.07%
• clamp＝0.10% → 资金费率0.01%

3/3 为什么值得关注？

HIP-3 已覆盖股票、指数、商品和 Pre-IPO 等市场，各类资产的交易时段、定价和对冲条件都有差异。

现在，部署方有了更多空间，针对不同资产平衡持仓成本与价格纠偏力度。

Hyperliquid🫡

这就是对应 rwa 现货未来可能要拆股、并股、股票分红、分拆。

大家不要将 HyperEVM 当作通用 EVM 生态来看待。

jeff 经常提醒，HyperEVM 的真正定位应该是进入 HyperCore 的无许可接口。

因此，天赋的发挥是体现在 HyperEVM 对 HyperCore 原生能力的调用上。

这里有一个最直观的范例——

像 BounceTech @BounceTech 的思路是直接利用 HyperCore ⇆ HyperEVM 特性，推出了“杠杆代币”，将 Hyperliquid 的 perp 打包成 ERC-20 代币。

相当于把玩永续合约的过程都抽象化了，买币即开单子，还能弄成 DeFi 产品。

然而这里还有升级版玩法，Altfun @altdotfun 就索性基于 BounceTech，再叠加 Bonding Curve 机制，做了一个带杠杆版的 meme 发射平台。

这帖子爆了，可见大家“居安思危”的紧绷情绪有了宣泄口。

@tradexyz 最近的增长非常好，羽翼逐渐丰厚了，大家已经开始担心未来他飞走了怎么办…

很好的讨论议题，我也有些零碎想法——

1）TradeXYZ 的成功，其实是「HIP-3 + Builder」的成功。缺一不可，互相成就。

2）TradeXYZ 现在主要丰满的是市场份额，不是底层基建能力。

3）TradeXYZ 也不会为了「钱」而搬走，因为不存在更赚钱的地方。

4）要逼得 TradeXYZ 另起炉自己干，必须满足两个条件：Hyperliquid 金融之家已无法满足 xyz 野心/愿景、且能力＞野心。

5）因此故事的发展可能取决于 Hyperliquid 的战略眼光、迭代速度、以及 TradeXYZ 的野心与能力。

6）现在讨论尚早，TradeXYZ 才刚开始长毛，远没到存量博弈阶段。大家居安思危，还是低估了 RWA perp 的天花板。

7）藤蔓长得快不快，要看基因与土壤；藤蔓长得高不高，还得看「墙」。@HyperliquidX 只管砌又高又厚的墙，让上面长满藤蔓。

As a HYPE bull during the Cambrian explosion of RWA perps, you should ask yourself the following questions:

1) if TradeXYZ left Hyperliquid tomorrow and launched their own exchange, where would you go to trade RWA perps?

2) if TradeXYZ launched a stock/token, how would you value HYPE differently?

3) what is the likelihood of #1 and #2?

I don’t intend to be a bear, but I’m pretty confident in my answers to #1 and #2 and I’m not naive enough to say I (or seemingly any major allocator) knows the answer to #3.

And before the .hl’s whine in my comments, this is not meant to slight either protocol, it’s to state a fact: TradeXYZ holds a large and growing amount of leverage over Hyperliquid.

这应该是 Hyperliquid 主动游说监管的最高规格了。

昨天发起了与 SEC Crypto Task Force (负责加密资产监管的政策工作组) 对话会议，具体讨论——加密资产监管的应对路径。

根据 SEC 的内部会议记录，这次领头的应该是 @HyperliquidR，Jeff、iliensinc 和 TradeXYZ 核心成员都有参会，“随行”的还有顶级律所 S&C 的四位律师。

Hyperliquid 相关代表还专门带上了附加文档 (Hyperliquid 协议的技术、市场和生态概述)，与 SEC 在会上进行了讨论。

虽然还不知道会议中达成了什么实质性结论，但这个举措本身就代表了积极的信号，越沟通越清晰。另一方面是，HRC 成立后也的确很有作为，充分动用了资源与人脉，已经给 @HyperliquidX 打通了直接与监管对话的路径。
